title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 27 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 27 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 27 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 27.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 27, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Jotham's reign is introduced in the first verse of the chapter, specifically in 2 Chronicles 27:1.

questions.question: How old was Jotham when he began to reign?
questions.explanation: Jotham was twenty and five years old when he began to reign according to 2 Chronicles 27:1.

questions.question: How long did Jotham reign in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: He reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem as stated in 2 Chronicles 27:1.

questions.question: What was the name of Jotham's mother?
questions.explanation: His mother's name is mentioned as Jerushah in 2 Chronicles 27:1.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 27, who did Jotham follow in doing what was right in the sight of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Jotham did that which was right according to all that his father Uzziah did, as stated in 2 Chronicles 27:2.

questions.question: What did Jotham NOT do during his reign?

questions.correctAnswer: Enter into the temple of the LORD
questions.explanation: The text states that Jotham entered not into the temple of the LORD in 2 Chronicles 27:2.

questions.question: What did the people do during Jotham's reign?
questions.explanation: The verse mentions that the people did yet corruptly during Jotham's reign in 2 Chronicles 27:2.

questions.question: What did Jotham build as part of his accomplishments?
options: The high gate of the house of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: The high gate of the house of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jotham built the high gate of the house of the LORD as stated in 2 Chronicles 27:3.

questions.question: Where did Jotham build much during his reign?

questions.question: Was Jotham's reign considered good in the sight of the LORD?
questions.explanation: Jotham did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, indicating his reign was viewed positively, as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 27:2.

questions.question: True or False: Jotham was the son of Uzziah.
questions.explanation: Jotham is referred to as the son of Uzziah in the context of his actions and reign in 2 Chronicles 27:2.

questions.explanation: The text mentions that Jotham built the high gate and worked on the wall of Ophel, but it does not state that he built a new temple, as per 2 Chronicles 27:3.

questions.question: True or False: The people followed Jotham's example fully.
questions.explanation: The verse states that the people did yet corruptly, indicating they did not follow Jotham's example fully, as stated in 2 Chronicles 27:2.

medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 27 to real-life situations.

options: They will be honored by men
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 27:6 states that Jotham became mighty because he prepared his ways before the LORD.

questions.question: Who did Jotham fight against?

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 27:2 indicate about Jotham's actions?
options: He did what was right in the sight of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: He did what was right in the sight of the LORD
questions.explanation: According to 2 Chronicles 27:2, Jotham did what was right in the sight of the LORD.

questions.question: What did the children of Ammon give Jotham in payment?
questions.explanation: The children of Ammon gave Jotham an hundred talents of silver, as stated in 2 Chronicles 27:5.

questions.question: What was Jotham's mother's name?

questions.explanation: Jotham did what was right in the sight of the LORD, indicating he sought the LORD, as stated in 2 Chronicles 27:2.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 27 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 27.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 27:7, where are the rest of the acts of Jotham written?
options: In the book of the kings of Israel and Judah
In the book of the prophets
In the scrolls of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: In the book of the kings of Israel and Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 27:7 explicitly states that the rest of Jotham's acts are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

questions.question: At what age did Jotham begin to reign according to 2 Chronicles 27:8?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 27:8 notes that Jotham was twenty-five years old when he began to reign.

questions.question: How many years did Jotham reign in Jerusalem as stated in 2 Chronicles 27:8?
questions.explanation: According to 2 Chronicles 27:8, Jotham reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Where was Jotham buried according to 2 Chronicles 27:9?
options: In the royal tombs of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 27:9 states that Jotham was buried in the city of David.

questions.question: Who succeeded Jotham as king according to 2 Chronicles 27:9?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 27:9 clearly states that Ahaz, Jotham's son, reigned in his stead.

questions.question: Which phrase in 2 Chronicles 27:7 indicates that Jotham's wars and ways are recorded elsewhere?
options: Lo, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah
He prepared his ways before the LORD
He did that which was right in the sight of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Lo, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 27:7 uses the phrase 'lo, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah' to indicate additional records exist.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'shafan' in 2 Chronicles 27:3 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'shafan' (שָׁפָן) in 2 Chronicles 27:3 is typically translated as 'rock hyrax,' a small, rock-dwelling animal, indicating the rocky terrain of Ophel.

questions.question: Which literary device is most evident in the phrase 'he prepared his ways before the LORD' in 2 Chronicles 27:6?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'he prepared his ways before the LORD' in 2 Chronicles 27:6 functions as foreshadowing of Jotham's success and favor from God.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of Jotham's righteous reign in 2 Chronicles 27:2?
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 15:33 also records Jotham's reign and notes he did right in the sight of the LORD, paralleling 2 Chronicles 27:2.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse echoes the theme of preparing one’s ways before God as found in 2 Chronicles 27:6?
questions.explanation: Matthew 3:3 quotes Isaiah about preparing the way of the Lord, echoing the theme in 2 Chronicles 27:6 of preparing one's ways before God.

questions.question: What immediately precedes 2 Chronicles 27:7 in the chapter?
options: Jotham’s victories and the tribute from the children of Ammon
His building of cities and castles
His age at the start of his reign
questions.correctAnswer: Jotham’s victories and the tribute from the children of Ammon
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 27:5 and 27:6 describe Jotham's wars and the tribute he received, which directly precede verse 7.

questions.question: Which literary device is seen in the structure of 2 Chronicles 27:2 comparing Jotham's deeds to his father Uzziah?
questions.explanation: The comparison to his father Uzziah in 2 Chronicles 27:2 forms an inclusio framing Jotham’s reign within the legacy of his predecessor.

questions.question: How does the term 'slept with his fathers' in 2 Chronicles 27:9 typologically connect with New Testament language about death?
options: It is a euphemism for death, similar to how the New Testament describes believers as 'sleeping' before resurrection
It refers to literal sleeping habits
It is a phrase unique to Chronicles with no NT connection
questions.correctAnswer: It is a euphemism for death, similar to how the New Testament describes believers as 'sleeping' before resurrection
questions.explanation: The phrase 'slept with his fathers' in 2 Chronicles 27:9 is a Hebrew idiom for death, paralleling the New Testament use of 'sleep' as a metaphor for death (e.g., 1 Thessalonians 4:13).

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 27:8, Jotham reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 27:8 explicitly states that Jotham reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: 2 Chronicles 27:2 states that Jotham entered the temple of the LORD during his reign.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 27:2 states explicitly that Jotham did not enter the temple of the LORD.

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 27 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 27 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 27:2 teach about human sin and sanctification?
options: Human sanctification is imperfect and coexists with ongoing corruption
Human sin is completely eradicated in the righteous
Sanctification guarantees social and political perfection
Human beings can enter God's presence without mediation
questions.correctAnswer: Human sanctification is imperfect and coexists with ongoing corruption
questions.explanation: Verse 2 states that Jotham did what was right but the people were still corrupt, showing sanctification is a progressive, imperfect reality alongside persistent sin.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine blessing and human responsibility does 2 Chronicles 27:6 teach?
options: God blesses those who prepare their ways before Him
Blessing is automatic and unrelated to human conduct
Human effort alone secures divine blessing
Blessing is given only after perfect obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses those who prepare their ways before Him
questions.explanation: Verse 6 shows Jotham’s mightiness resulted from preparing his ways before the LORD, emphasizing cooperation between divine blessing and human responsibility.

questions.question: What doctrine about the relationship between earthly power and divine approval is taught in 2 Chronicles 27:5?
options: God grants military success to those He approves
Military victory depends solely on human strategy
God is indifferent to earthly political power
questions.correctAnswer: God grants military success to those He approves
questions.explanation: Verse 5 recounts Jotham’s victory over Ammonites and their tribute, implying divine sanction of his reign and military success.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 27:3 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 shows Jotham building the temple gates and walls, reflecting God's providential care over His house and people.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 27:6 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 declares Jotham was mighty because God prepared the way before him, illustrating God's sovereign power over history.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 27:9 connect to the broader biblical theme of dynastic succession and covenant continuity?
options: It shows God's covenant faithfulness through legitimate dynastic transfer
It rejects dynastic succession as irrelevant to God's plan
It predicts the end of the Davidic line
It emphasizes individual merit over family lineage
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God's covenant faithfulness through legitimate dynastic transfer
questions.explanation: Verse 9 records Jotham’s burial and the succession of Ahaz, affirming continuity of the Davidic covenant.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does the tribute from Ammon in 2 Chronicles 27:5 foreshadow?
options: The gathering of Gentiles into God's kingdom
The rejection of Israel by surrounding nations
The universal curse on nations opposing God
questions.correctAnswer: The gathering of Gentiles into God's kingdom
questions.explanation: The tribute from a foreign nation (Ammon) points to the inclusion of Gentiles in God's redemptive plan.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 2 and 6 teach about sanctification and divine blessing?
options: Sanctification is a process where God blesses those who faithfully seek Him despite human imperfection
Perfect sanctification is required for blessing
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification is a process where God blesses those who faithfully seek Him despite human imperfection
questions.explanation: Verse 2 notes ongoing corruption despite right doing, and verse 6 shows blessings upon preparation before God, combining imperfection with divine favor.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 27:3 and 27:4 teach about the relationship between divine worship and social order?
options: Building and strengthening religious and civic infrastructure reflects holistic devotion to God
Worship and social order are unrelated
Religious building projects distract from social concerns
Civic construction is superior to religious devotion
questions.correctAnswer: Building and strengthening religious and civic infrastructure reflects holistic devotion to God
questions.explanation: Verse 3 describes temple construction, verse 4 civic fortifications, implying integrated worship and social stability.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 27:5 and 27:6 teach about divine justice and human warfare?
options: God grants just victory to those who prepare and align with His will
War is always unjust regardless of outcome
Human military might is independent of divine justice
Victory is purely chance without divine involvement
questions.correctAnswer: God grants just victory to those who prepare and align with His will
questions.explanation: Verse 5 records military success, and verse 6 attributes might to divine preparation, linking justice and victory.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that 2 Chronicles 27:2-6 promotes an uncritical view of monarchy despite the people’s corruption. What does the text actually teach?
options: The text acknowledges imperfect human sanctification but affirms divine blessing on righteous leadership
The text ignores human corruption and idealizes kingship
The text condemns all monarchy as corrupt
The text claims the people were perfectly righteous
questions.correctAnswer: The text acknowledges imperfect human sanctification but affirms divine blessing on righteous leadership
questions.explanation: Verses 2 and 6 note people’s corruption but also Jotham’s right doing and divine blessing, showing balanced evaluation.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s covenant faithfulness is emphasized in 2 Chronicles 27:1?
options: God’s covenant promises extend through dynastic lineage
God’s covenant is unconditional and unrelated to lineage
Covenant faithfulness depends on individual merit only
The covenant was broken with each new king
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant promises extend through dynastic lineage
questions.explanation: Verse 1 mentions Jotham’s mother and father, highlighting genealogical continuity in God’s covenant.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified in 2 Chronicles 27:9 with respect to the king’s death and succession?
questions.explanation: The peaceful succession after Jotham’s death in verse 9 reflects God’s faithfulness to His covenant promises.

questions.question: How do 2 Chronicles 27:7 and 2 Chronicles 27:8 together teach about the reliability of biblical historiography?
options: They affirm that historical accounts are preserved accurately in the book of kings
They dismiss historical record-keeping as unreliable
They show contradictions within biblical history
They negate the importance of genealogical records
questions.correctAnswer: They affirm that historical accounts are preserved accurately in the book of kings
questions.explanation: Verse 7 refers to detailed records in the book of kings, and verse 8 repeats reign details, affirming historiographical reliability.

questions.question: What theological synthesis do 2 Chronicles 27:4 and 2 Chronicles 27:5 provide concerning divine-human cooperation in leadership?
options: Effective leadership involves both building societal structures and trusting God for victory
Human effort alone determines leadership success
Divine intervention negates the need for human planning
Military conquest is unrelated to governance
questions.correctAnswer: Effective leadership involves both building societal structures and trusting God for victory
questions.explanation: Verse 4 shows structural building, and verse 5 military success, together indicating cooperation of human effort and divine blessing.
